Theme 062 · Signature directions

Mascot Agent

The agent becomes a character: a round teal body with two white oval eyes, born from the coral dot of the Acme mark on the drop. It never talks — it looks, blinks, squashes and cheers — and all of its expression lives in the eyes. The team’s dashboard does the computing; the mascot peeks over its edge and hands what it finds to a human.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Mascot body — teal ellipse with a soft top-left highlight; distinct from the logo — no face is ever added to the mark
  • Eye kit — neutral · focus (narrow) · alarm (wide) · happy (arcs) · blink — the only expressions
  • Squash & stretch — ±16 % from the base, volume preserved; landings always on a beat, shadow scales with it
  • Gaze line — dotted arc from the eyes to the target (anomaly cell, CTA)
  • Hands — two small round nubs that appear only when gripping or holding
  • Onion skin — faded previous poses along the path — storyboard only; plays as real motion in production

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Birth arc — dot → body along a bezier over 3 beats (1.5 s at 120 BPM), stretch 1.3 on the way, squash 0.84 on landing, back.out(2)
  • Eye tracking — eyes translate ≤ 0.3 r toward the active column, power2.out 0.2 s, one move per beat
  • Blink + hop — blink = eye scaleY 1 → 0.1 → 1 in 0.12 s on off-beats; hop = y −40 px + squash in 0.35 s landing on the downbeat

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

A character makes an invisible background agent lovable and memorable, and eye-only acting keeps it calm and trustworthy rather than cartoonish. Risk: mascots can trivialise a serious product and are expensive to animate well; keep the acting minimal and never let the character do the human’s job.

Adapt to your product: Derive the character from a shape in your own mark (a dot, a corner, a letter counter) without altering the logo itself, and give it one job: pointing the human to what matters.

References: https://blog.duolingo.com/world-character-visemes/ (how Duolingo animates its characters with state-driven poses) · https://www.creativebloq.com/advice/understand-the-12-principles-of-animation (squash & stretch and the 12 principles of animation)
